extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting to Taylor & Francis journals (and journal editors/publishers interested in open research policies)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on Taylor & Francis about Open Science Badges and related Transparency and Openness Promotion (TOP) standards, including eligibility, application steps, and what each badge/standard expects. Also general orientation to TOP standards for improving reporting of data, materials, code, preregistration, and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data (TOP standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards on Data speak to the items generated over the course of the study and how you should preserve or share them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented to increase clarity into underlying research data and materials; intended to improve scientific reporting so that underlying research data are available for verification and reuse. TOP standards may be applied at increasing rigor (disclosure, requirement, verification). Editors checking badge applications will verify that the URL points to a recognized repository rather than just figures or summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials (TOP standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards on Materials speak to the items generated over the course of the study and how you should preserve or share them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on ensuring research materials are preserved/shared so others can reproduce or extend the work; like the Data standard, it can be implemented at levels of disclosure, requirement, or verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical Code Transparency (TOP standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard on Analytical Code Transparency speaks to the items generated over the course of the study (code) and how you should preserve or share them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages sharing of analysis code to support reproducibility; can be implemented as disclosure, requirement, or verification depending on journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and Analysis Transparency (TOP standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard on Design and Analysis Transparency points to discipline-specific reporting guidelines that remind authors to report key methodological details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires authors to report key methodological details following discipline-specific guidance so that studies can be properly evaluated and replicated; may be operationalized at different levels of rigor by journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration (TOP standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Preregistration standards emphasize the importance of keeping two modes of research distinct: exploratory research (which seeks to make new discoveries and find unexpected trends) and confirmatory research (the purpose of which is to test a specific hypothesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages preregistration of study designs and analysis plans to distinguish confirmatory from exploratory work; TOP implementation levels (disclosure/requirement/verification) determine how strictly journals enforce or check preregistration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication (TOP standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Replication standard makes it clear that direct replications are an important contribution to science, even though they’re traditionally harder to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes and encourages publication and appropriate reporting of replication studies as part of improving scientific robustness; journals can adopt policies to better support replications.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOP implementation levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the TOP standards can be implemented in one of three levels of increasing rigor: disclosure, requirement, or verification of the mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tiers allow journals to begin with lighter-touch policies (disclosure) and progressively adopt stronger requirements or independent verification; serves as a roadmap for policy improvement over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Data badge (COS/Open Science Badges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes that authors have shared data: the badge signals to the reader that the content of the study (data) has been made available in perpetuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers submit an open practices disclosure form and, if accepted, the badge is displayed in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. Editors will check that the URL points to a recognized repository (to avoid cases where authors claim data are available but only present figures or summaries). Authors must meet the Open Science Badges criteria set out by the Center for Open Science (COS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Materials badge (COS/Open Science Badges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes that authors have shared materials used in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may apply during submission via the open practices disclosure form; editors assess the submission against COS criteria and, if accepted, display the badge. Materials should be preserved in an appropriate repository to meet the intent of the badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistered / Preregistered Analysis Plan badge (COS/Open Science Badges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes that the study or analysis plan was preregistered prior to conducting the research/analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes separation between exploratory and confirmatory research; authors apply via the disclosure form and editors verify preregistration against COS criteria. The badge signals that hypotheses or analysis plans were pre-specified and archived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badge application process and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers submitting to journals that support the COS initiative have the opportunity to apply for one or more of the badges during submission and must meet the Open Science Badges criteria in order to earn a badge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon submission authors receive an email with details of badges offered, links to additional information, an open practices disclosure form, and the editor’s email. To apply, complete the disclosure form and email it back to the editor; the editor will assess the submission against COS criteria. You may apply for more than one badge but must meet the criteria for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal participation indicator / Author checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor & Francis journals that have adopted the Open Science Badges initiative display a notice in the journal’s header on Taylor & Francis Online and advise authors to read the journal’s 'Instructions for Authors' for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the journal header or Instructions for Authors to confirm participation; the publisher also provides a quick guide and links to further resources (open access publishing guide, data sharing guides, ethics) to assist compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badge intent: improve real data sharing quality (anti-pattern warning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Badging is associated with higher rates of data sharing and higher quality of data sharing; a common anti-pattern is authors stating data are available while only providing figures or summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The badge criteria and editorial checks (e.g., repository URL verification) are intended to prevent superficial claims of availability; authors should deposit full datasets/materials/code in recognized repositories rather than rely on summarized/figure-only representations.
